The zone of proximal
development (ZPD) is a
concept from
psychologist Lev
Vygotsky, referring to
the range of tasks a
learner can perform with
guidance but not yet
independently.

It’s the "sweet spot" for
learning, where
challenges are within
reach with support,
encouraging growth and
skill development.
